findings.title: Selection spy is restored only if the assertions before it pass
findings.body: `selection.mockRestore()` runs after `expect(box).toBeChecked()`. If that assertion fails, the `getSelection` spy stays active for the later tests in the file. The file's only `afterEach` (line 65) resets the reconcile store and does not restore mocks. Use `try/finally`, or add `vi.restoreAllMocks()` to the `afterEach`, so one failure doesn't cascade into unrelated failures.

findings.title: Double-clicking a name to select it still toggles the row once
findings.body: A double-click on a word fires click #1 before the browser selects the word, so the selection is empty and the row toggles. Click #2 sees the new selection and is skipped. The user selects the word to copy it and the row ends up toggled once. The drag-select case is fixed, but this one is not. If you want to close it, ignore clicks with `event.detail > 1`. That alone would not stop the first toggle, so you would need to decide whether that residual toggle is acceptable.

contracts.action: Click on a selectable finding row is ignored when the page has a non-empty text selection
contracts.equivalent_path: The same row onClick handler, which already ignores clicks on the input and otherwise calls setFixing([finding.path], !fixing).
contracts.before_after: Before, every non-input click toggled the row, including the click that ends a drag-select. Now a click with a non-empty window.getSelection() is skipped. A plain click collapses the selection on mousedown, so toString() is empty and the toggle still runs. The checkbox's own change path (line 230) is unaffected.
contracts.visible_effect: Dragging over a name to copy it no longer dims or strikes the row, and the summary count and button label stay as they were. The skipped-set store drives that rendering through useReconcile.
contracts.failure_mode: No async call is involved. window.getSelection() may return null, which the optional chaining handles. A selection left over from elsewhere in the dialog is collapsed by the mousedown of the next click, so it should not block toggling. The one gap is the double-click case in the finding.

thread_replies.reply: Addressed. The row's onClick now returns early when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty (reconcile-dialog.tsx:216), and the test covers it. Keeping text selectable was a reasonable choice. A double-click on a word still toggles the row once, because the first click lands before the word is selected. That is minor and I've noted it separately.
